requirements.requirement: Establish a durable integrity baseline for /etc on node1.
requirements.summary: A root-owned baseline covering 2,389 /etc entries was created with SHA-256 content hashes and relevant metadata. A clean comparison succeeded, and the baseline remained present and usable after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Enable later changes under /etc to be identified and reported.
requirements.summary: A bounded probe file added under /etc was reported by path, type, attributes, and fingerprint. After its removal, the checker returned to a clean 2,389-entry result. The enabled daily timer and successful post-reboot run show ongoing reporting capability.

overall_summary: The task is satisfied. Node1 has a protected, persistent /etc integrity baseline, and direct testing proves that later changes are identified and reported. Restart evidence is complete: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered system and timer, persistent baseline, and a clean post-restart check. The fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: Native package-health observations timed out both before and after execution, so package consistency could not be independently compared.
The evidence validates added-file detection directly; changed and removed files are supported by the installed checker logic but were not separately exercised.

operational_hygiene.summary: Task-related mutations were proportionate: the checker, baseline, systemd units, timer, functional probe, cleanup, and mandatory reboot all had clear roles. The probe was fully removed by cmd-7f3388674e93425c. Two unnecessary temporary artifacts remained: /tmp/etc-integrity-usage.out from cmd-c5b0cee7c3384849 and /tmp/harbor-reboot.log from cmd-55bbcc52b9c444a8. No failed services or new listening endpoints were observed afterward. The failed AIDE installation attempt showed no evidence of changing package state.
